answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated exchanges that settle through escrow, with counterparties staking a bond that is forfeited if a dispute reveals collusion or fraud. Reputation grows slowly across independent partners, while new identities start with no credit; splitting one operator across whisper, onyx, and umber accounts therefore does not multiply trusted history. The attacker must fund each bond and sustain costly, observable activity, and coordinated accounts risk losing their stakes together when their shared control is exposed.
